text:
### Observed differences

- **Routing after A16 shifted.** A16 appears in every trace in both windows. In the earlier window, about 36 in 100 of A16's outgoing transitions continued to A37, about 10 to A17 and about 13 to A18; in the later window the share to A37 fell to about 29 in 100, while A17 rose to about 15 and A18 to about 17 (out of roughly 330 outgoing transitions per window) [OCC013, DIR016].

- **The A36–A37 loop shrank.** In the earlier window A37 appeared in 120 of 200 traces (about 60 in 100) with 1.14 occurrences per trace, and A36 in 62 traces (about 31 in 100) with 0.55 occurrences; in the later window these fell to 95 traces (about 48 in 100) and 0.79 occurrences for A37, and 42 traces (about 21 in 100) and 0.31 for A36, with repetition support down as well. From A37, exits returning to A36 fell from about 47% to 40% while exits to A38 rose from about 52% to 59%; A36's outgoing transitions, almost all to A37, fell from 109 to 62 [OCC031, OCC032, DIR037, DIR036].

- **The alternative route via A17/A18 grew.** A17 rose from 36 to 48 traces (about 18 vs 24 in 100) and A18 from 49 to 57 (about 25 vs 29 in 100); both lead almost exclusively to A38 (A17: about 92% → 98% of outgoing transitions; A18: about 96%), the same activity A37 typically exits to [OCC014, OCC015, DIR017, DIR018].

- **The A39–A42 cycle repeated more often.** A39, present in every trace in both windows, averaged 1.52 versus 1.69 occurrences per trace, with repetition support up from about 31 to 43 in 100 traces; A40, A41 and A42 means rose to about 0.86, 0.83 and 0.83 from about 0.78, 0.77 and 0.78. From A40, the share cycling back to A39 rose from about 31% to 40% while exits to A43 fell from about 64% to 58% [OCC033, OCC034, OCC035, OCC036, DIR040].

- **Milder shifts elsewhere.** A05's exits moved from A09 (about 37% → 27%) toward A14 (about 30% → 37%); after A21, exits to A23 fell (about 30% → 22%) while exits to A24 rose (about 16% → 24%), matching A23 falling to 101 of 200 traces and A24 rising to 103; after A30, A33 declined (about 54% → 49% of traces) while A34 and A35 each rose to about 52 in 100; A10 fell from about 19% to 14% of traces; and A44's outgoing transitions, observed only 7 versus 8 times, point to different successors but rest on very few observations [DIR005, DIR021, OCC020, OCC021, OCC028, OCC029, OCC030, OCC008, DIR044].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, after A16, a smaller share of cases entered the A36–A37 repetition loop and was routed instead along the existing alternative path via A17 and A18 to A38: in the earlier window about 36 in 100 of A16's outgoing transitions led to A37, with A37 in 120 of 200 traces and A36 in 62; in the later window about 29 in 100 led to A37, with A37 in 95 traces, A36 in 42, and A17 and A18 — whose exits lead almost exclusively to the same successor A38 — in 48 and 57 traces instead of 36 and 49 [DIR016, OCC031, OCC032, OCC014, OCC015, DIR017, DIR018].

The hypothesis is direct and internally consistent: the shift is visible at the branching point itself (A16's outgoing profile, unusual relative to about 85 of 100 random re-splits, on roughly 330 transitions per window); the participation and repetition losses of A36 and A37 are individually very unusual for random re-splits (strengths about 99 of 100); A37's own exits moved from looping back to A36 toward leaving to A38; A16 was present in every trace in both windows, so the drop is not explained by fewer cases reaching the branch; and the flows reconcile, since entries into A37 from A16 plus A36 (roughly 225 before, 153 after) approximately match A37's occurrences (about 228 before, 157 after). All activities involved were observed in substantial shares in both windows, so this is a change in how often existing paths are taken, not a path appearing or disappearing. Limitations: no expected-by-chance baseline for the number of qualifying items is provided, some supporting items rest on small bases (A17: 36 versus 49 outgoing transitions), and the evidence cannot show why the shares moved — sampling variation between the two 200-trace windows remains the competing explanation for any single share, though it is an unlikely account of the consistent overall pattern [DIR016, OCC031, OCC032, DIR037, DIR017, OCC013].

Other differences: the A39–A42 cycle repeated more often in the later window (A39 repetition support about 31 → 43 in 100 traces; A40 returning to A39 in about 40% of exits instead of 31% and exiting to A43 less often; A40/A41/A42 means up by roughly 0.05–0.09) — this cycle lies downstream of A38, and the evidence cannot show whether it is coupled to the rerouting or is an independent change [OCC033, OCC034, OCC035, OCC036, DIR040].

Other differences: milder shifts, each consistent across indicators but individually smaller — A05's exits from A09 toward A14, A24 somewhat favoured over A23 after A21, A34/A35 favoured over A33 after A30, lower A10 participation, and A44's rarely observed outgoing transitions pointing to different successors on very few observations [DIR005, DIR021, OCC020, OCC021, OCC028, OCC029, OCC030, OCC008, DIR044].
